units.title: Verbal and Written Communication
units.topics: • Developing artist statements that articulate the concepts, processes, and intentions behind artworks. • Practicing oral presentation skills for critiquing sessions, exhibitions, and academic discussions. • Learning to write proposals and descriptions for exhibitions, grants, and competitions.

units.title: Exhibition Planning and Public Engagement
units.topics: • Understanding the logistics of organizing an art exhibition, including space planning and installation. • Exploring strategies for engaging audiences through talks, workshops, and social media. 23 • Collaborating with peers to plan and execute group exhibitions or art events.

units.title: Foundations of Environmental Studies
units.topics: • Multidisciplinary Nature: Understanding the integration of physical, biological, and social sciences in environmental studies. • Scope and Importance: Exploring the significance of environmental education and its role in sustainable 24 development. • Public Awareness: Recognizing the need for community involvement and awareness in addressing environmental issues.

units.title: Natural Resources and Ecosystems
units.topics: • Natural Resources: o Renewable Resources: Exploration of resources like solar, wind, and biomass energy. o Non-renewable Resources: Study of fossil fuels, minerals, and their environmental impacts. • Ecosystems: o Structure and Function: Analyzing the components and processes within ecosystems. o Energy Flow and Nutrient Cycles: Understanding how energy and nutrients move through ecological systems. • Biodiversity and Conservation: o Levels of Biodiversity: Examining genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity. o Conservation Strategies: Evaluating methods for preserving biodiversity and natural habitats.

units.title: Human Impact and Environmental Management
units.topics: • Environmental Pollution: o Types of Pollution: Air, water, soil, and noise pollution and their sources. o Effects and Control Measures: Assessing the impacts of pollution and strategies for mitigation. • Social Issues and the Environment: o Urbanization and Industrialization: Investigating how societal development affects the environment. o Environmental Ethics and Policies: Understanding the role of ethics and legislation in environmental protection. • Human Population and the Environment: o Population Growth: Studying the relationship between population dynamics and environmental stress. o Resource Consumption: Analyzing how human activities influence resource depletion. • Field Work: o Practical Exposure: Engaging in field visits to observe environmental issues firsthand.

units.title: Cybercrime and Cyber Law
units.topics: • Understanding Cybercrime: Exploration of various cyber offenses such as hacking, identity theft, financial fraud, and cyberbullying. • Legal Frameworks: Study of national and international laws 26 addressing cybercrime, including the Information Technology Act and its implications. • Case Studies: Analysis of real-world cybercrime incidents to understand legal proceedings and enforcement challenges.

units.title: Social Media and E-Commerce Security
units.topics: • Social Media Risks: Identification of threats like phishing, impersonation, and data breaches on platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. • E-Commerce Vulnerabilities: Examination of security issues in online shopping and digital payment systems, including fraud prevention measures. • Best Practices: Guidelines for secure usage of social media and e-commerce platforms, emphasizing privacy settings and transaction safety.

units.title: Digital Devices Security and Cyber security Tools
units.topics: • Device Protection: Strategies for securing computers, smartphones, and its devices against malware and unauthorized access. • Cyber security Tools: Introduction to antivirus software, firewalls, encryption technologies, and multi-factor authentication methods. • Emerging Technologies: Overview of advanced cyber security solutions like AI-driven threat detection and block chain-based security protocols.

units.title: Exploring Historical Sites and Museums
units.topics: • Objective: Investigate the role of historical sites and museums in preserving and presenting art and cultural heritage. • Focus Areas: o Analyze the architecture and design of museums and galleries. o Study the curation and display methods employed in exhibitions. o Examine the impact of these institutions on public engagement with art.

units.title: Art Centers, Artist Studios, and Art Fairs
units.topics: • Objective: Examine the function and influence of art centers, artist studios, and art fairs on contemporary art practice. • Focus Areas: o Explore the collaborative environment of art centers and their role in fostering creativity. o Investigate how artist studios contribute to the development of individual artistic styles. o Assess the significance of art fairs in promoting artists and connecting them with audiences. 28

units.title: Biannual Exhibitions and Art Competitions
units.topics: • Objective: Analyze the role of biannual exhibitions and art competitions in the professional development of artists. • Focus Areas: o Study the themes and selection processes of major art competitions. o Evaluate the opportunities these events provide for exposure and career advancement. o Investigate the impact of such events on the art market and public perception of art.

units.topics: • Detailed study of cranial landmarks and their influence on form. • Understanding age, gender, and ethnic variations in head structure. • Breakdown of complex head angles and dynamic poses.

units.title: Texture and Skin Detailing
units.topics: • Rendering skin tones and textures with various mediums. • Techniques for depicting wrinkles, pores, and subtle facial details. • Studying the effects of lighting on different skin types and tones.

units.title: Master Studies and Creative Interpretation
units.topics: • Analyzing portrait techniques of master artists. • Exploring stylization versus realism in head study. • Creating expressive and conceptual head studies based on imagination.

units.title: Advanced Figure Construction
units.topics: • Breaking down the figure into geometric shapes for better structure. • Studying dynamic poses and weight distribution. • Exploring exaggeration and stylization for expressive figure drawing.

units.title: Drapery and Clothing Study
units.topics: • Understanding the behavior of fabric on the human body. • Studying different types of folds (pipe, zigzag, spiral, and inert folds). • Rendering textures and patterns in clothing through shading techniques.

units.title: Composition and Spatial Awareness
units.topics: • Placing figures within a background for narrative storytelling. • Exploring perspective and depth in life drawing. • Creating balanced compositions with multiple figures in a scene.

units.title: Symbolism and Narrative in Still Life
units.topics: • Explore how objects in still life compositions can convey deeper meanings, cultural references, or personal narratives. • Study historical and contemporary examples to understand the use of symbolism in still life art.

units.title: Advanced Techniques: Mediums and Surfaces
units.topics: • Experiment with various painting mediums such as oil, acrylic, and watercolor, and their application on different surfaces like canvas, wood, or paper. • Learn techniques like glazing, impasto, and dry brush to achieve desired textures and effects.

units.title: Contemporary Approaches to Still Life 20
units.topics: 32 • Investigate modern interpretations of still life, including abstract, minimalistic, and mixed-media approaches. • Encourage personal expression and innovation by integrating unconventional materials or digital elements into still life compositions

units.title: Visual Storytelling and Concept Development
units.topics: • Explore how to convey narratives and concepts through visual elements in design. • Study techniques for developing compelling stories and 33 messages within pictorial compositions

units.title: Typography and Text Integration
units.topics: • Understand the role of typography in pictorial design and how to effectively integrate text with images. • Learn about font selection, hierarchy, and the interplay between textual and visual elements.

units.title: Digital Media and Mixed Techniques
units.topics: • Experiment with digital tools and software to create and manipulate pictorial designs. • Combine traditional and digital methods to develop mixed- media artworks that push creative boundaries.

units.title: Romanesque Art
units.topics: • Study of Mosaics in France, Manuscripts and Handbook Covers, and Decorative Objects. • Examination of period, purpose, subjects, material features, trade, religion, and development plans in Romanesque art.

units.title: Gothic Art

units.title: The Renaissance Period
units.topics: • Study of key artists: o Sculptors: Niccolò dell'Arca, Donatello, Michelangelo. o Painters: Giotto di Bondone, Masaccio, Sandro Botticelli, Andrea Mantegna, Leonardo da Vinci, Raphael. o Architect: Filippo Brunelleschi. • Analysis of religious symbolism, representation, narration, and emerging artistic techniques such as sfumato, chiaroscuro, perspective, foreshortening, and proportion.

units.title: Mannerism
units.topics: o Painters: Agnolo Bronzino, Giovanni Bellini, Titian, Tintoretto. 35 o Sculptor: Giovanni da Bologna. • Examination of Mannerism’s distinct stylistic elements, exaggerated forms, and dramatic compositions.

units.topics: • Exploration of the Renaissance movement in other parts of Europe, focusing on key artists: o Jan van Eyck, Rogier van der Weyden, Albrecht Dürer, Pieter Bruegel the Elder, El Greco, and Hans Memling. • Study of the historical development of Western painting, including its societal, cultural, political, and economic influences.

units.title: Introduction to Rasa Theory
units.topics: • Definition, nature, and scope of Rasa in Indian aesthetics. • Understanding poetry as an expression of emotive meaning. • The validity of Rasa as a theoretical concept in art and literature. • An introduction to Natyasastra as the foundational text of Indian aesthetics. • Exploration of the term Rasa and Rasa Sutra (terms, values, purpose, and mode of creation). 7.5

units.title: The Four Commentators of Rasa-Sutra
units.topics: • Abhinavagupta’s significant contributions to Rasa theory. • Bhatta Lolatta’s Utpattivada (theory of Rasa as a psychological state). • Sri Sankuka’s Anumitivada (theory of inference in aesthetic experience). • Bhatta Nayaka’s Bhuktivada (theory of aesthetic enjoyment and transcendence). 7.5

units.title: Navarasa and Rasa-Vighna
units.topics: • Study of the nine Rasas (Navarasa) and their significance in artistic expression. • Analysis of factors that enhance or hinder the experience of Rasa (Rasa-Vighna). 7.5

units.title: Dhvani-Siddhanta and Poetic Theories
units.topics: • Dhvani (suggestion) as the essence of poetry. • Key literary concepts: o Alankara (figures of speech). o Auchitya (propriety and appropriateness in artistic expression). o Riti (style and poetic diction). 7.5

units.title: Advanced Multi-block and Reduction Printing
units.topics: • Techniques of multi-color printing using multiple blocks or reduction method. • Understanding registration and layering of colors. • Exploring visual rhythm and harmony through color planning.

units.title: Texture and Surface Experimentation
units.topics: • Creating visual texture using various carving tools and materials. 38 • Incorporating natural and found textures in relief blocks. • Enhancing expressive quality of prints through surface variation.

units.title: Creative Composition and Concept Development
units.topics: • Developing personal themes and narratives in relief prints. • Planning layout and design for aesthetic impact. • Integrating visual storytelling with relief printing techniques.

units.title: Print Aesthetics and Composition
units.topics: • Principles of design, texture, and contrast in printmaking. • Experimentation with layering, color application, and editioning techniques.

units.title: Physical Fitness, Wellness & Lifestyle
units.topics: • Meaning & Importance: Understanding the significance of maintaining physical fitness and wellness for overall health and quality of life. • Components of Physical Fitness: o Cardiovascular Endurance: The ability of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen during sustained physical activity. o Muscular Strength: The maximum amount of force a muscle or group of muscles can generate. o Muscular Endurance: The ability of a muscle to continue to perform without fatigue. o Flexibility: The range of motion available at a joint. o Body Composition: The proportion of fat and non-fat mass in the body. • Components of Wellness: o Physical Wellness: Regular physical activity and proper nutrition. o Emotional Wellness: Understanding and managing feelings. o Social Wellness: Developing a sense of connection and belonging. o Intellectual Wellness: Engaging in creative and stimulating mental activities. o Spiritual Wellness: Seeking meaning and purpose in human existence. 12.5

units.title: Yoga
units.topics: • Meaning & Importance: Yoga is a mind-body practice that combines physical postures, breathing exercises, and meditation to promote overall health and well-being. • Elements of Yoga: o Asanas: Physical postures that improve flexibility, strength, and balance. 12.5 41 o Pranayama: Breathing techniques that enhance respiratory function and mental clarity. o Meditation: Mental exercises that promote relaxation and mindfulness. • Introduction to Key Asanas: o Sukhasana: Easy Pose, promotes relaxation and meditation. o Tadasana: Mountain Pose, improves posture and balance. o Padmasana: Lotus Pose, enhances meditation and flexibility. o Shashankasana: Rabbit Pose, stretches the spine and calms the mind. o Naukasana: Boat Pose, strengthens the core and improves digestion. o Vrikshasana: Tree Pose, enhances balance and concentration. o Garudasana: Eagle Pose, improves focus and balance
